question.problem: Find where the tangent to the curve $y={x}^{5}+2$ at the point $(-1,1)$ intersects the $x$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)={x}^{5}+2.$ Let's first calculate the derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{5}+2)=5{x}^{4}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the slope of the tangent at our point is

$$
\begin{aligned}m={f}^{′}(-1)=5(-1)^{4}=5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the tangent is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-1 & =5(x+1) \\ y & =5x+5+1 \\ y & =5x+6.\end{aligned}
$$

To find where the tangent line intercepts the $x$-axis, we set $y=0$ and solve:

$$
\begin{aligned}0 & =5x+6 \\ x & =-\frac{6}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the point of intersection is $(-\frac{6}{5},0).$
